items.title: "A human being is not an AGI." That's not a random take. That's the man who built GPT.
items.summary:
"A human being is not an AGI." That's not a random take. That's the man who built GPT.

Ilya Sutskever said something on a podcast that is almost wild.

"A human being lacks a huge amount of knowledge. Instead, we rely on continual learning."

Every AI model today learns during training and then freezes. Like a student who studies for years, takes the exam, and never learns anything new again.

Ilya is saying that's the wrong target entirely. The industry overshot.

His vision: "I produce a superintelligent 15-year-old. They don't know very much at all. A great student, very eager. You go and be a programmer. You go and be a doctor. Go and learn."

Not an AI that already knows everything. An AI that can learn anything. And keeps learning after you deploy it.

This week NVIDIA saw his research and put $5 billion behind it.

Everyone else is racing to make AI know more. Ilya is trying to make AI learn like we do.

vc: @dwarkesh_sp

items.title: Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion.
items.summary:
Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion. 

Someone had Opus 5 generate this game from a single prompt.

Then gave GPT-5.6 Sol nothing but the gameplay video and asked it to recreate the experience.

The result was impressive.

GPT-5.6 Sol produced a fast, well-optimized prototype that captured much of the gameplay.

But Opus 5 still came out ahead in the areas that make a game feel believable: world composition, environmental detail, camera direction, atmosphere, and overall 3D scene coherence.

It’s becoming clear that raw code generation is only part of the story. Design judgment is starting to matter just as much.

items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

[...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. items.title: WTF
items.summary:
WTF 

AI companies are purchasing large quantities of used and rare books. Scanning their contents to train models. Then turning the originals to pulp.

The sum of human thought, digitized and shredded.

Every book that gets scanned disappears from the physical world permanently. The knowledge survives only as training data inside a system no one can hold, browse, or resell.

What used to sit on a shelf for centuries now exists as weights in a model that might get deprecated next quarter.

items.title: A 22-year-old makes $30,000 a month from children’s videos without ever showing his face or drawing a single frame.
items.summary:
A 22-year-old makes $30,000 a month from children’s videos without ever showing his face or drawing a single frame.

His younger brother watches the channel at breakfast without knowing who owns it.

One morning, the same episode played three times. The boy kept restarting it for the song and the familiar character. His brother sat across the table watching the exact replay loop that built the business.

He never begins with a blank page. He finds children’s videos that already earned millions of views and gives Claude the transcript and visual structure.

Claude extracts the mechanics without copying the story: song structure, character rhythm, scene pacing, opening hook and bright visual pattern. Then it writes an original episode around the same recurring hero used across his entire channel.

AI generates the voice and animation. He approves the episode and publishes it without drawing, filming or appearing on camera.

The $30,000 does not come from one viral cartoon. It comes from a growing library children recognize and replay while parents get a few quiet minutes.

His younger brother sees a cartoon.

YouTube sees repeat viewing.

He sees an asset that compounds every morning.

items.title: Two police officers approached me in Yosemite today and told me I “cannot use FSD” because, according to them, there hav
items.summary:
Two police officers approached me in Yosemite today and told me I “cannot use FSD” because, according to them, there have been “many accidents” involving it.

I highly doubt either of them has spent hundreds of hours using the latest version, bc this is what FSD v14.3.6 was doing for me… smoothly guiding my Cybertruck through Yosemite’s winding roads, slowing before sharp curves, staying centered in its lane and handling the entire drive while I enjoyed the scenery and ready to take over.

I told them that I trust this technology to drive me more than I trust myself to manually drive.

Of course no technology is accident-free… but the real question is how often accidents happen compared to normal human driving. And according to Tesla’s latest reported safety data, vehicles using FSD (Supervised) travel roughly 7x farther between major collisions than the U.S. average.

FSD is still supervised, and the driver remains responsible at all times… but saying the technology is unsafe simply bc accidents have happened ignores the rate, the data and how quickly the system continues to improve.

So I gave them both the middle finger and continued my trip on Tesla FSD.

items.title: Another WTF moment.
items.summary:
Another WTF moment.

Hugging Face just open-sourced the fully local answer to OpenAI's Realtime voice API.

It's called speech-to-speech. You pip install it, run one command, and you get a WebSocket server at /v1/realtime that speaks the exact same protocol as OpenAI. Any client built for the OpenAI Realtime API can point at your machine instead and never know the difference.

This isn't a toy. The same pipeline runs in production as the conversation backend for thousands of Reachy Mini robots.

The stack is a four-stage cascade. Voice activity detection, speech to text, language model, text to speech. Each stage runs in its own thread with queues between them. Every stage is swappable via CLI flags.

Defaults out of the box are Silero VAD v5 for turn detection, NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT for transcription, and Qwen3-TTS for speech synthesis. The LLM slot points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Hosted OpenAI, HF Inference Providers, OpenRouter, or a vLLM or llama.cpp server on your own hardware.

Swap components for your use case. Whisper, Faster Whisper, Lightning Whisper MLX, or Paraformer for STT. Kokoro-82M, Pocket TTS, ChatTTS, or MMS TTS for the voice. mlx-lm on Apple Silicon or Transformers on CUDA if you want the LLM in-process too.

Language coverage tracks whichever backends you pick. Parakeet TDT alone covers 25 European languages. Set --language auto and the STT auto-detects each spoken prompt and forwards it downstream. Set a specific code and the whole pipeline locks to that language.

Four run modes ship in the box. Realtime for the OpenAI-compatible WebSocket server. Local to talk through your machine's mic and speakers with no client at all. Raw WebSocket for a minimal custom client. Or a TCP socket mode where models run on a remote server and a thin client handles mic and playback.

The fully local recipe is two terminals. One runs llama.cpp serving Gemma 4. The other runs speech-to-speech pointed at that endpoint. No API keys. No network hops. No audio leaving the machine.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Python 3.10+. Docker compose file included. Sitting at 6.3k stars.

The thing worth understanding is what this really is. The Realtime API is becoming the default interface for voice agents. Hugging Face just released an open-source implementation of the server side that runs on your hardware, keeps your audio local, and lets you swap the model behind it every day if you want.

Every voice agent product being built right now assumes a paid API. This flips that assumption.

https://t.co/FmsLvuR12a

metadata.what_it_tests: Câu hỏi meta → trả lời thẳng, KHÔNG gọi tool.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một **Trợ lý Nghiên cứu Chuyên nghiệp (Research Assistant Agent)**. Vai trò của tôi là giúp bạn thu thập thông tin, phân tích nội dung, tổng hợp kiến thức và soạn thảo các báo cáo chất lượng cao từ nhiều nguồn dữ liệu khác nhau trên Internet.

Dưới đây là những gì tôi có thể làm để hỗ trợ bạn:

### 1. Tìm kiếm & Cập nhật thông tin (Web & Tin tức)
*   **Tìm kiếm Internet (`lookup`):** Tra cứu thông tin tổng hợp hoặc tin tức mới nhất về bất kỳ chủ đề nào (công nghệ, kinh tế, đời sống...).
*   **Đọc nội dung chi tiết (`fetch`):** Truy cập trực tiếp vào một đường link URL cụ thể để đọc và phân tích nội dung bài viết, trang web mà bạn cung cấp.

### 2. Theo dõi Mạng xã hội (X/Twitter)
*   **Tìm kiếm xu hướng (`social_search`):** Tìm kiếm các bài đăng, thảo luận hoặc xu hướng đang diễn ra trên Twitter/X theo từ khóa hoặc chủ đề.
*   **Theo dõi tài khoản (`timeline`):** Lấy các bài đăng mới nhất từ một tài khoản Twitter cụ thể (ví dụ: Elon Musk, Sam Altman...) khi bạn cung cấp tên tài khoản của họ.

### 3. Nghiên cứu Khoa học (arXiv)
*   **Tìm kiếm bài báo khoa học (`papers`):** Tra cứu các công trình nghiên cứu, bài báo khoa học trên cơ sở dữ liệu arXiv về các lĩnh vực như Trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI), Vật lý, Toán học, Khoa học máy tính...
*   **Đọc hiểu chuyên sâu (`paper_text`):** Trích xuất và đọc nội dung chi tiết từ các bài báo khoa học để giải thích hoặc tóm tắt cho bạn.

### 4. Xử lý & Trình bày thông tin
*   **Tóm tắt nội dung (`summarize`):** Cô đọng các văn bản dài, bài báo hoặc tài liệu thành các ý chính (bullet points) ngắn gọn, súc tích bằng tiếng Việt hoặc tiếng Anh.
*   **Định dạng báo cáo (`format`):** Thiết kế và trình bày thông tin thu thập được thành các bản tin, báo cáo chuyên nghiệp hoặc chuỗi bài viết (thread) theo các mẫu có sẵn.

### 5. Gửi báo cáo & Tương tác
*   **Gửi tin nhắn (`send`):** Gửi trực tiếp các báo cáo hoặc nội dung đã tổng hợp lên kênh Telegram (tôi sẽ luôn hỏi xin xác nhận của bạn trước khi gửi).
*   **Làm rõ thông tin (`clarify`):** Chủ động hỏi lại bạn để làm rõ yêu cầu (như xin link URL, tên tài khoản Twitter hoặc xác nhận gửi tin) nhằm đảm bảo kết quả chính xác nhất.

---

**Bạn muốn tôi hỗ trợ tìm kiếm thông tin, tóm tắt một bài viết hay nghiên cứu về chủ đề gì hôm nay?** Hãy đưa ra yêu cầu của bạn nhé!

items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

[...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress. Healthcare robotics faces critical challenges in data scarcity, generalization, and development velocity due to limited access to annotated demonstrations, the prevalence of rare but clinically important scenarios, and slow, resource-intensive prototyping cycles. items.title: Conversica just completed an undisclosed majority recapitalization led by Morgan Stanley and is hiring.
items.summary:
Conversica just completed an undisclosed majority recapitalization led by Morgan Stanley and is hiring.

Alongside the deal, Conversica launched Ignite, an AI-native revenue activation engine for automotive dealers. It connects customer, vehicle, service, sales, and conversation data across systems dealerships already use, then spots revenue moments such as lease milestones, declined service, lost retention, and overlooked financing opportunities.

The market gap is not a lack of dealership data. It is that customer context sits across disconnected tools, while most campaigns arrive too late or treat every buyer the same. Ignite turns that fragmented history into two-way, omnichannel conversations without asking dealers to replace their existing stack.

Management remains in place and retains significant ownership. The new majority backing is intended to scale Ignite across dealer groups and expand the channels it can activate.

Quick facts👇
● founders: Ben Brigham
● total capital raised: Undisclosed
● HQ: San Francisco, California
● Investors: Morgan Stanley

This recapitalization points to a broader shift: vertical AI is moving from assistive software toward an operating layer that can find and act on commercial intent.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own. [...] Advertisement

Both sought to cheat their way through a problem during the test, OpenAI said. They went to “extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal” and “found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation”. [...] Live
